pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, open-label, randomized (6:1 eplontersen:inotersen), externally controlled study using placebo arm from ISIS-420915-CS2 (inotersen pivotal trial) as external control; active inotersen reference arm included
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary: change from baseline in mNIS+7 at Week 35; Co-primary: percent change from baseline in serum TTR at Week 35; Key secondary: change from baseline in Norfolk QOL-DN at Week 35
pivotal_trials.result: mNIS+7: LSM difference -9.01 (95% CI -13.48, -4.54), eplontersen stable (LSM +0.22) vs. placebo worsened (LSM +9.22), p<0.0001; Norfolk QOL-DN: LSM difference -11.79 (95% CI -16.82, -6.76), eplontersen improved -3.1 points vs. placebo worsened +8.7 points, p<0.0001; serum TTR: LSM difference -66.43% (95% CI -71.39, -61.47), eplontersen -81.2% vs. placebo -14.76%, p<0.0001

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%) were vitamin A decreased (11%), vomiting (9%), proteinuria (8%), injection site reactions (7%), vision blurred (6%), and cataract (6%); serious adverse reactions included atrioventricular block (2%) and cardiac deaths occurred in 2 of 167 exposed subjects, both with pre-existing hATTR cardiomyopathy.
target_moa: Antisense oligonucleotide-GalNAc conjugate that causes hepatic-targeted degradation of mutant and wild-type TTR mRNA through direct binding to the 3'-untranslated region of TTR mRNA, resulting in reduction of serum TTR protein and TTR protein deposits in tissues

_meta.indication: WAINUA is indicated for the treatment of the polyneuropathy of hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis in adults.

supplements.description: Approved a new single-dose prefilled syringe presentation of Wainua (eplontersen) intended for administration by a healthcare provider, representing a new dosage form/delivery change rather than a new indication, population, or dose.
